ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
(Tracked-Changes Redline — Lender/Secured Party Markup of Counterparty Draft)

Document Status: COUNTERPARTY DRAFT MARKED AGAINST INTERNAL PLAYBOOK, EXECUTED CREDIT AGREEMENT, DEPOSITORY BANK STANDARD FORM, ACCOUNT DETAILS, AND RELATED CORRESPONDENCE/CHECKLISTS
Parties (as corrected): 
  Debtor/Pledgor: [Borrower Affiliate — Account Holder] ("Pledgor")
  Secured Party: [Administrative Agent], as Administrative Agent for the Lenders under the Credit Agreement ("Secured Party")
  Bank: [Depository Bank] ("Bank")
Accounts: See Schedule I (as corrected)
Governing Credit Agreement: Credit Agreement dated as of [CA Date] among [Borrower], the Lenders party thereto, and [Administrative Agent], as Administrative Agent (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the "Credit Agreement")
Redline Legend: [DELETE] = deletion from counterparty draft; [INSERT] = insertion required by playbook/Credit Agreement/bank form; [MOVE] = relocation; [COMMENT] = drafting note for negotiation (not operative text)

================================================================================
PREAMBLE / RECITALS
================================================================================

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is entered into as of [Effective Date], by and among:

(i) [INSERT full legal name of Account Holder / Pledgor], a [jurisdiction] [entity type] (the "Pledgor");

(ii) [INSERT full legal name of Administrative Agent], as Administrative Agent for the Secured Parties under the Credit Agreement (in such capacity, together with its successors and assigns in such capacity, the "Secured Party"); and

(iii) [INSERT full legal name of Depository Bank], a [jurisdiction] [entity type] (the "Bank").

[DELETE counterparty's unilateral "Customer / Bank only" framing and any characterization of Secured Party as a mere "notice party" or "interested third party."]

RECITALS

WHEREAS, the Pledgor has established with the Bank the deposit account(s) and, if applicable, securities account(s) identified on Schedule I hereto (each, an "Account" and collectively, the "Accounts");

WHEREAS, pursuant to the Credit Agreement and the [Security Agreement / Pledge Agreement] dated as of [SA Date] (as amended, restated, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time, the "Security Agreement"), the Pledgor has granted to the Secured Party a security interest in, among other things, the Accounts and all cash, financial assets, securities entitlements, instruments, investment property, and other property credited thereto or carried therein from time to time, and all proceeds thereof (collectively, the "Collateral");

WHEREAS, the parties are entering into this Agreement to perfect the Secured Party's security interest in the Accounts by "control" within the meaning of Sections 9-104 and/or 8-106 and 9-106 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of New York (the "UCC"), and to set forth the rights and obligations of the parties with respect to the Accounts; and

WHEREAS, the Bank is willing to enter into this Agreement on the terms and conditions set forth herein.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements herein contained, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:

================================================================================
ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
================================================================================

Section 1.1  Definitions.  Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings ascribed to them in the Credit Agreement or the Security Agreement, as applicable.  As used herein:

"Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or other day on which commercial banks in New York, New York [INSERT: or the city in which the Bank's office maintaining the Accounts is located] are authorized or required by law to close.

"Entitlement Order" has the meaning set forth in Section 8-102(a)(8) of the UCC (and, with respect to a deposit account, includes any instruction directing disposition of funds in such deposit account).

"Notice of Exclusive Control" or "NOEC" means a written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank substantially in the form of Exhibit A hereto (or such other form as the Bank and Secured Party may reasonably agree), stating that the Secured Party is exercising exclusive control over the Accounts.

"Permitted Instructions" means, prior to the Bank's receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control, instructions originated by the Pledgor with respect to the disposition of funds or financial assets in the Accounts, subject to Section 2.3 and any standing instructions or blocked-account mechanics agreed in writing among the parties.

"UCC" means the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect from time to time in the State of New York; provided that, if by reason of mandatory provisions of law, perfection, the effect of perfection or non-perfection, or priority of the security interest in any Collateral is governed by the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in a jurisdiction other than New York, "UCC" means the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in such other jurisdiction for purposes of the provisions hereof relating to such perfection, effect of perfection or non-perfection, or priority.

[INSERT playbook-required definitions: "Credit Agreement," "Security Agreement," "Loan Documents," "Event of Default," "Obligations," "Secured Parties," "Lenders," and cross-reference that Event of Default and related terms are determined under the Credit Agreement without independent Bank inquiry obligation as to underlying defaults except as expressly set forth herein.]

Section 1.2  Rules of Construction.  [INSERT standard construction rules consistent with Credit Agreement Section 1.02: including, without limitation, that headings are for convenience only; "including" means "including without limitation"; references to Articles/Sections/Exhibits/Schedules are to this Agreement unless otherwise indicated; and that this Agreement is a "Loan Document" under the Credit Agreement.]

================================================================================
ARTICLE II — THE ACCOUNTS; CONTROL
================================================================================

Section 2.1  Identification of Accounts; Account Details.
(a) The Bank confirms that Schedule I correctly identifies each Account by account number, account title, account type (deposit account / securities account), and office location.  [DELETE any counterparty draft language permitting "accounts as the Customer may designate from time to time" without Secured Party consent and updated Schedule I.]
(b) [INSERT] The Pledgor shall not establish any additional account at the Bank that is intended to be subject to this Agreement, or change the account number or title of any Account, without the prior written consent of the Secured Party and prompt delivery of an updated Schedule I executed (or acknowledged) by the Bank and the Secured Party.
(c) [INSERT — playbook / account-details checklist] The account title for each Account shall be in the form: "[Pledgor Name] — [Administrative Agent Name], as Secured Party" or such other form as the Secured Party may reasonably require to evidence the security interest, subject to the Bank's reasonable account-titling conventions.
(d) [INSERT] The Bank represents and warrants that (i) each Account is a "deposit account" and/or "securities account" (as applicable) as defined in the UCC, (ii) the Bank is a "bank" and/or "securities intermediary" (as applicable) with respect to each Account, and (iii) the jurisdiction of the Bank for purposes of UCC Sections 9-304 and/or 8-110 and 9-305 is the State of New York [or other agreed jurisdiction matching Credit Agreement collateral opinions].

Section 2.2  Security Interest; Acknowledgment of Control.
(a) The Pledgor confirms that it has granted to the Secured Party a security interest in the Collateral pursuant to the Security Agreement.
(b) The Bank acknowledges the security interest of the Secured Party in the Accounts and the Collateral.
(c) [INSERT — core control covenant; delete counterparty "acknowledgment only" watered-down language] The Bank agrees that it will comply with Entitlement Orders and instructions originated by the Secured Party directing disposition of funds in the Accounts without further consent by the Pledgor.  The parties intend that the Secured Party have "control" of each Account within the meaning of UCC §§ 9-104(a)(2) (deposit accounts) and/or 8-106(d)(2) and 9-106 (securities accounts).  This Agreement constitutes authentic evidence of such control arrangement.
(d) [DELETE counterparty provision conditioning Bank compliance with Secured Party instructions on (i) Bank's independent verification of an Event of Default, (ii) joint instruction of Pledgor and Secured Party after NOEC, or (iii) a cure/notice period running in favor of Pledgor after NOEC before exclusive control is effective.]
(e) [INSERT] The Bank's obligation to comply with the Secured Party's Entitlement Orders is absolute and unconditional under this Section 2.2 and Article III, and the Bank shall have no duty to inquire into the authority of the Secured Party to issue any Entitlement Order or the existence of an Event of Default or other underlying circumstance, except as expressly provided in Section 3.3 with respect to the form of NOEC.

Section 2.3  Pledgor Access Prior to Notice of Exclusive Control.
(a) Until the Bank receives a Notice of Exclusive Control from the Secured Party, the Pledgor may operate the Accounts and originate Permitted Instructions in the ordinary course, [INSERT playbook qualifier:] subject to (i) any cash dominion, blocked account, or springing control mechanics required under the Credit Agreement, (ii) any standing wire/ACH instructions agreed in writing among the parties, and (iii) the restrictions in Section 2.4.
(b) [INSERT — Credit Agreement alignment] If the Credit Agreement provides for springing cash dominion upon a specified trigger (including Excess Availability, Dominion Event, or Event of Default), the Secured Party may deliver a Notice of Exclusive Control upon such trigger in accordance with the Credit Agreement, and the Bank shall honor the same without independent investigation of the trigger.
(c) [DELETE counterparty "Pledgor retains exclusive dominion and control until Bank receives final non-appealable judgment" or similar litigation-conditioned control language — off-market and fatal to perfection/priority analysis.]

Section 2.4  Restrictions on Accounts.
[INSERT playbook-required negative covenants as to Accounts:]
(a) The Pledgor shall not permit any Account to become subject to any other control agreement, pledge, encumbrance, or third-party claim, other than (i) the security interest of the Secured Party and (ii) Banker's Liens permitted under Section 5.1.
(b) The Pledgor shall not close any Account without the prior written consent of the Secured Party.
(c) The Pledgor shall not change the account type in a manner that would adversely affect perfection by control without the prior written consent of the Secured Party and appropriate amendments hereto.
(d) [INSERT] No Account shall be a "consumer account" or maintained primarily for personal, family, or household purposes.

Section 2.5  Subordination of Bank's Rights; Priority.
(a) [INSERT — critical playbook item; replace counterparty broad banker setoff free-for-all] The Bank subordinates any security interest, lien, right of setoff, right of recoupment, or other claim it may have in or against the Accounts or the Collateral to the security interest of the Secured Party, except for the limited Banker's Liens described in Section 5.1.
(b) The Bank agrees that the Secured Party's security interest in the Accounts has priority over any lien or claim of the Bank, other than Banker's Liens to the limited extent set forth in Section 5.1.
(c) [DELETE counterparty language preserving unfettered setoff for "any obligations owing to Bank from time to time, whether or not related to the Accounts."]

================================================================================
ARTICLE III — NOTICE OF EXCLUSIVE CONTROL; EXCLUSIVE CONTROL PERIOD
================================================================================

Section 3.1  Delivery of Notice of Exclusive Control.
(a) The Secured Party may deliver a Notice of Exclusive Control to the Bank at any time.  [DELETE counterparty requirement that NOEC may be delivered "only following an Event of Default that is continuing and only after X Business Days' prior written notice to Pledgor," to the extent inconsistent with Credit Agreement cash dominion / remedy provisions.  Playbook position: Secured Party discretion; no Bank gatekeeping; Pledgor notice is a Secured Party/Pledgor matter under the Loan Documents, not a condition to Bank honor.]
(b) [INSERT] A Notice of Exclusive Control shall be deemed received by the Bank upon the earlier of (i) actual receipt at the address and in the manner specified in Section 8.1 and Schedule II, and (ii) if sent by email to the notice contacts in Schedule II with confirmed transmission, [INSERT playbook timing:] 12:00 noon (New York time) on the next Business Day if sent after 2:00 p.m. or on a non-Business Day; otherwise on the Business Day of transmission, unless the Bank's standard form requires a longer effective time not to exceed one (1) Business Day after actual receipt, in which case such Bank-standard outside time may apply solely as to operational implementation (not as a substantive cure right for Pledgor).

Section 3.2  Effect of Notice of Exclusive Control.
(a) From and after the Bank's receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control, and until the Bank receives a written rescission of such Notice of Exclusive Control from the Secured Party:
    (i) the Bank shall comply solely with Entitlement Orders and instructions originated by the Secured Party concerning the Accounts and shall cease complying with instructions originated by the Pledgor;
    (ii) the Pledgor shall have no further right to withdraw, transfer, or otherwise direct disposition of funds or financial assets in the Accounts; and
    (iii) the Bank shall not honor checks, wires, ACH entries, or other payment orders originated by the Pledgor, except as the Secured Party may expressly direct in writing.
(b) [DELETE counterparty "dual signature" or "Pledgor counter-notice stays exclusive control" mechanics.]
(c) [INSERT] The Bank shall promptly (and in any event within one (1) Business Day) confirm in writing to the Secured Party its receipt of any Notice of Exclusive Control and the time of receipt.

Section 3.3  Form; No Duty to Investigate.
(a) The Bank may rely on any Notice of Exclusive Control that appears on its face to be signed by an authorized person of the Secured Party (including by PDF or electronic signature) and need not investigate the truth or accuracy of any statement therein or the authority of the signer, beyond the Bank's commercially reasonable authentication procedures consistent with its standard form.
(b) [INSERT] Concurrently with or promptly after delivery of a Notice of Exclusive Control to the Bank, the Secured Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to deliver a copy to the Pledgor; provided that failure to deliver such copy shall not affect the validity or effectiveness of the Notice of Exclusive Control as against the Bank or the Pledgor, or the Bank's obligation to comply therewith.

Section 3.4  Rescission.
Only the Secured Party may rescind a Notice of Exclusive Control, by written notice to the Bank.  [DELETE any Pledgor unilateral rescission or automatic lapse provisions.]

================================================================================
ARTICLE IV — BANK DUTIES AND STANDARD OF CARE
================================================================================

Section 4.1  Duties Limited.
The Bank undertakes only those duties expressly set forth herein.  Without limiting the foregoing, the Bank shall not be deemed a fiduciary for the Secured Party or the Pledgor by reason of this Agreement, except to the extent the Bank acts as a securities intermediary with respect to a securities account (in which case its duties are as set forth in UCC Article 8 and herein).

Section 4.2  Standard of Care.
The Bank shall perform its obligations hereunder with the same degree of care that it exercises with respect to comparable accounts for its other commercial customers, [INSERT:] and in any event not less than commercially reasonable care.  [DELETE counterparty "gross negligence or willful misconduct only" standard if used to dilute ordinary care for ministerial account operations — accept gross negligence/willful misconduct as the liability standard for monetary damages if consistent with Bank standard form, while preserving commercially reasonable care as the performance standard.]

Section 4.3  Permitted Reliance.
The Bank may rely on notices and Entitlement Orders it reasonably believes to be genuine and authorized, and on advice of counsel.  [INSERT carve-in:] provided that such reliance shall not excuse non-compliance with a facially proper Notice of Exclusive Control or Secured Party Entitlement Order under Article III.

Section 4.4  Statements and Information.
[INSERT playbook requirement:] The Bank shall provide to the Secured Party, at the Secured Party's expense if so required by Bank's standard fee schedule (provided fees are disclosed on Schedule III), copies of periodic account statements and, upon reasonable request, other account information with respect to the Accounts, including transaction detail and available balances, substantially concurrently with delivery to the Pledgor or promptly upon request.  The Pledgor hereby authorizes such disclosure.

Section 4.5  No Obligation to Advance / Overdrafts.
The Bank shall have no obligation to permit overdrafts or to extend credit in respect of any Account.  [INSERT:] If the Bank nonetheless permits an overdraft or extension, any resulting claim is subject to Section 5.1 limitations and subordination.

Section 4.6  Force Majeure.
[Accept Bank standard force majeure for operational inability, INSERT:] provided that the Bank shall use commercially reasonable efforts to resume performance and shall promptly notify the Secured Party of any event that materially impairs the Bank's ability to comply with Entitlement Orders.

================================================================================
ARTICLE V — BANKER'S LIENS, FEES, AND INDEMNITY
================================================================================

Section 5.1  Limited Banker's Liens.
(a) [INSERT playbook-required limited carve-out replacing counterparty unlimited setoff:] The Bank may retain its lien on and right of setoff against the Accounts solely for (i) its customary fees and charges for the maintenance and operation of the Accounts, (ii) the face amount of items deposited to an Account and returned unpaid, reverse ACH entries, and similar chargebacks, and (iii) overdrafts created in the ordinary course on the Accounts, in each case incurred in respect of the Accounts themselves (collectively, "Banker's Liens").
(b) Banker's Liens shall not secure any other obligations of the Pledgor or any affiliate to the Bank, including loans, derivatives, card exposure, or other credit products, whether or not related to the Accounts.
(c) The aggregate amount subject to Banker's Liens under clause (a)(i) shall not exceed the Bank's published or scheduled fees for a period of [INSERT: thirty (30) / ninety (90) days], unless otherwise agreed in Schedule III.
(d) Upon receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control, the Bank shall not exercise setoff in respect of Banker's Liens without concurrent written notice to the Secured Party, and shall cooperate in good faith to quantify outstanding Banker's Liens.

Section 5.2  Fees.
Fees for the Accounts and for this Agreement shall be as set forth on Schedule III or the Bank's standard fee schedule disclosed to the parties.  [INSERT:] Prior to a Notice of Exclusive Control, fees may be debited to the Accounts.  After a Notice of Exclusive Control, fees shall be paid by the Pledgor (or as the Secured Party may direct) and the Bank shall not debit the Accounts for fees without the Secured Party's consent, except for ordinary maintenance fees disclosed on Schedule III not to exceed $[_] per month per Account unless otherwise agreed.

Section 5.3  Indemnity; Limitation of Liability.
(a) The Pledgor shall indemnify the Bank against losses arising from the Bank's performance hereunder, except to the extent resulting from the Bank's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or material breach of this Agreement.  [Negotiate allocation consistent with Bank standard form and Credit Agreement borrower indemnity.]
(b) [INSERT Secured Party-protective limitation:] The Secured Party shall have no indemnity obligation to the Bank except to the extent of the Secured Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, and any such obligation shall be limited to actual direct damages (excluding consequential, special, or punitive damages), consistent with the Credit Agreement's agent exculpation standards.
(c) [DELETE counterparty draft requiring Secured Party to indemnify Bank on the same basis as Pledgor, or making Secured Party jointly and severally liable for all Bank fees and chargebacks.]
(d) [INSERT] Neither the Bank's exculpation nor any indemnity in favor of the Bank shall impair the Secured Party's perfection by control or the Bank's absolute duty to comply with Articles II and III.

================================================================================
ARTICLE VI — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
================================================================================

Section 6.1  Pledgor Representations.
The Pledgor represents and warrants to the Secured Party and the Bank that: (a) it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization; (b) it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement and has taken all necessary action to authorize the same; (c) this Agreement constitutes its legal, valid, and binding obligation, enforceable against it in accordance with its terms; (d) it is the sole account holder of each Account free and clear of liens other than the Secured Party's security interest and permitted Banker's Liens; (e) the execution and performance of this Agreement do not conflict with law, its organizational documents, or material agreements; and (f) [INSERT] each Account is maintained for business/commercial purposes only.

Section 6.2  Bank Representations.
The Bank represents and warrants that: (a) it is a [bank / securities intermediary] duly organized and validly existing; (b) it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (c) this Agreement has been duly authorized and constitutes its legal, valid, and binding obligation; (d) [INSERT control-critical reps from playbook and bank form comparison:] it maintains each Account as set forth on Schedule I; (e) it has not entered into any currently effective control agreement or similar arrangement with respect to any Account in favor of any person other than the Secured Party; and (f) the person executing this Agreement on behalf of the Bank is authorized to bind the Bank with respect to the Accounts.

Section 6.3  Secured Party Representations.
The Secured Party represents that the person executing this Agreement and any Notice of Exclusive Control on its behalf is authorized to do so.  [DELETE expansive Secured Party reps regarding enforceability of the Credit Agreement, non-contravention, or solvency — off-market for an administrative agent in an ACA.]

================================================================================
ARTICLE VII — TERMINATION; SURVIVAL
================================================================================

Section 7.1  Termination.
(a) This Agreement shall terminate upon the earliest of:
    (i) written notice from the Secured Party to the Bank that all Obligations have been paid in full and all commitments terminated (or that the Secured Party otherwise releases its security interest in the Accounts), and instruction to terminate;
    (ii) written agreement of the Secured Party, the Pledgor, and the Bank; or
    (iii) [INSERT limited Bank termination right consistent with bank standard form:] the Bank's resignation as depository upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the Pledgor and the Secured Party; provided that (A) the Bank shall continue to comply with this Agreement during the notice period, (B) the Pledgor and Secured Party may jointly designate a successor bank and replacement control agreement, and (C) the Bank shall transfer the balances in accordance with the Secured Party's Entitlement Orders (or, if no NOEC is in effect, joint instructions) on the effective resignation date.
(b) [DELETE counterparty unilateral Pledgor termination rights, and any Bank termination "for any reason on 5 days' notice" without transfer-of-control protections.]
(c) [DELETE automatic termination upon "closure of the Accounts by Customer" without Secured Party consent.]

Section 7.2  Effect of Termination.
Termination shall not affect rights and obligations accrued prior to termination, including indemnity, fee, and subordination provisions, which shall survive as applicable.  Upon termination under Section 7.1(a)(i), the Bank may resume honoring Pledgor instructions free of this Agreement's exclusive-control mechanics.

Section 7.3  Release Letters.
[INSERT] Promptly following termination under Section 7.1(a)(i), the Secured Party shall execute a customary release/termination letter reasonably acceptable to the Bank.

================================================================================
ARTICLE VIII — NOTICES
================================================================================

Section 8.1  Notices.
All notices, NOECs, Entitlement Orders, and other communications under this Agreement shall be in writing and delivered by hand, overnight courier, certified mail, or email (with PDF attachment) to the addresses and contacts set forth on Schedule II (as either party may update by notice to the others).  [INSERT playbook:] Email notice is effective as provided in Section 3.1 for NOECs and otherwise upon confirmed transmission during business hours on a Business Day.  The Bank's operational "callback" or authentication procedures for wires remain applicable to payment orders, but shall not delay recognition of a NOEC beyond the outside time in Section 3.1.

[DELETE counterparty exclusive requirement of hard-copy original wet-ink NOEC delivered only by certified mail as the sole effective method — unacceptable operational lag; permit email/PDF with commercially reasonable authentication.]

================================================================================
ARTICLE IX — MISCELLANEOUS
================================================================================

Section 9.1  Governing Law.
This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflicts-of-law principles that would require application of the laws of another jurisdiction; provided that perfection, the effect of perfection or non-perfection, and priority of security interests are governed as provided in the UCC definition in Section 1.1.  [ALIGN with Credit Agreement governing law and opinion jurisdictions; DELETE counterparty home-office law if inconsistent with NY UCC control opinions.]

Section 9.2  Jurisdiction; Waiver of Jury Trial.
[INSERT] Each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts sitting in the Borough of Manhattan, City of New York, and waives any objection based on venue or forum non conveniens.  EACH PARTY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT.  [Conform to Credit Agreement dispute-resolution provisions to the extent applicable to the agent and borrower-side parties; Bank may retain limited local-venue carve for collection of its fees if required by bank form — flag in memo.]

Section 9.3  Amendments.
No amendment or waiver of this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by the Bank, the Pledgor, and the Secured Party.  [DELETE counterparty "Bank and Customer may amend account terms without Secured Party consent" as applied to control, priority, setoff, or exclusive-control mechanics.]

Section 9.4  Successors and Assigns; Secured Party Replacement.
(a) This Agreement binds and benefits the parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns.
(b) [INSERT] The Secured Party may assign or transfer its rights hereunder to any successor Administrative Agent under the Credit Agreement without the Bank's or Pledgor's consent, upon written notice to the Bank and Pledgor.  The Bank shall recognize such successor upon receipt of customary evidence of appointment.
(c) The Pledgor may not assign its rights or obligations hereunder without the prior written consent of the Secured Party and the Bank.

Section 9.5  Counterparts; Electronic Signatures.
This Agreement may be executed in counterparts (including by PDF or DocuSign/electronic signature), each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which constitute one instrument.  Electronic signatures are authorized and effective.

Section 9.6  Entire Agreement; Conflict with Credit Agreement.
This Agreement, together with the Schedules and Exhibits hereto, constitutes the entire agreement among the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes prior agreements solely among these parties on such subject. ISSUES AND RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Draft Review

TO:      File / Deal Team / Client
FROM:    Counsel — Contracts / Banking
DATE:    [Closing Timeline Date]
RE:      Review of Counterparty Draft Account Control Agreement against Internal Playbook, Executed Credit Agreement, Depository Bank Standard Form, Account Details, and Related Correspondence/Checklists
MATTER:  Deal materials — contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
RELATED DELIVERABLE: aca-redline.docx (tracked-changes redline incorporating required modifications and insertions)

================================================================================
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

We reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement ("Draft ACA") for use in connection with the deposit/securities accounts that will constitute collateral under the executed Credit Agreement and related Security Agreement. The Draft ACA was tested against:

  (1) the firm's internal Account Control Agreement playbook (mandatory and preferred positions);
  (2) the executed Credit Agreement (including cash dominion, collateral, Loan Document, agency, and enforcement provisions);
  (3) the depository bank's standard form control agreement and operational policies;
  (4) the account-details checklist / bank setup materials; and
  (5) related correspondence and closing checklists (NOEC mechanics, perfection opinions, and collateral questionnaire items).

Bottom line: The Draft ACA, as proposed, does not reliably perfect a first-priority security interest by "control" under UCC §§ 9-104 / 8-106 and 9-106, and contains multiple off-market borrower- and bank-favorable deviations that create material priority, operational, and enforcement risk. We do not recommend execution of the Draft ACA without the modifications reflected in aca-redline.docx.

Highest-priority failures (must-fix before funding/rely-on-control):
  • Control covenant diluted to acknowledgment / joint instruction / litigation-conditioned mechanics (Issues 1–3)
  • Unfettered Bank setoff and non-subordinated banker liens (Issue 4)
  • NOEC timing, form, and Pledgor cure/stay rights that defeat springing or exclusive dominion (Issues 5–7)
  • Incomplete account identification, titling, and UCC jurisdiction representations (Issues 8–9)
  • Unilateral termination / account closure rights (Issue 10)
  • Secured Party indemnity and representation overreach (Issues 11–12)
  • Governing law / opinion mismatch risk (Issue 13)

Risk rating key used below:
  CRITICAL — Impairs perfection, priority, or core remedy; do not accept
  HIGH     — Material economic or enforcement exposure; push hard; limited fallback only with client sign-off
  MEDIUM   — Off-market or playbook deviation; negotiate; acceptable fallback available
  LOW      — Clean-up, consistency, or preference

================================================================================
II. SCOPE AND MATERIALS REVIEWED
================================================================================

A. Counterparty Draft ACA (primary markup paper).
B. Internal ACA Playbook — mandatory positions on: control language; NOEC; subordination of bank claims; limited banker's liens; termination; successor agent; Loan Document status; NY law; securities-intermediary add-on; irrevocability; account titling; information rights; Secured Party indemnity limits.
C. Executed Credit Agreement — definitions of Obligations, Event of Default, Administrative Agent, Secured Parties; cash dominion / blocked account / springing control triggers; collateral and perfection covenants; agency succession; governing law and forum; Loan Document construct; borrower notice provisions.
D. Security Agreement / Pledge Agreement — grant of security interest in deposit accounts, securities accounts, supporting obligations, and proceeds; control agreement delivery covenant.
E. Depository Bank standard form ACA and fee/ops schedules — authentication, NOEC implementation lag, force majeure, resignation, fee debit practices, authorized signatories.
F. Account details / checklist — account numbers, titles, ABA/branch, currency, deposit vs. securities account characterization, existing control agreements search, consumer-account screen.
G. Related correspondence — bank KYC and control-agreement unit contacts; opinion counsel checklist items on control and jurisdiction; closing checklist requiring fully executed ACA and Schedule I prior to funding.

================================================================================
III. LEGAL FRAMEWORK (BRIEF)
================================================================================

Perfection by control — deposit accounts. Under UCC § 9-104(a), a secured party has control of a deposit account if: (1) the secured party is the bank; (2) the debtor, secured party, and bank agree in an authenticated record that the bank will comply with instructions originated by the secured party directing disposition of funds in the account without further consent by the debtor; or (3) the secured party becomes the bank's customer. Priority among conflicting control interests is generally first-to-obtain-control (UCC § 9-327), subject to the bank's residual priority for certain claims unless subordinated.

Perfection by control — securities accounts / security entitlements. UCC §§ 8-106(d) and 9-106: control via agreement of the securities intermediary to comply with entitlement orders originated by the secured party without further consent of the entitlement holder.

Market structure of ACAs. Market ACAs separate (i) control for perfection from the Effective Date from (ii) operational exclusive dominion upon NOEC. Conflating the two — or conditioning Bank compliance on default verification, dual signatures, or litigation outcomes — is off-market for institutional syndicated credit facilities and is rejected by the playbook.

Credit Agreement overlay. The ACA must not cut back springing cash dominion or remedy rights the Lenders bargained for in the Credit Agreement. As between Pledgor and Secured Party, the Credit Agreement/Security Agreement control conflicts; the Bank is not charged with full Loan Document knowledge but must honor the four-corners control and NOEC mechanics.

================================================================================
IV. ISSUE-BY-ISSUE ANALYSIS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 1 — Missing / Diluted "Control" Covenant (UCC § 9-104(a)(2) / § 8-106(d)(2))
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Art. II (acknowledgment / "notice" framing); preamble characterizing Secured Party as interested third party
Playbook requirement: Express Bank covenant to comply with Secured Party entitlement orders/instructions directing disposition of funds/financial assets without further Pledgor consent; explicit statement that Secured Party has "control" under UCC §§ 9-104 and/or 8-106 & 9-106 from the Effective Date
Deviation:          Draft substitutes acknowledgment of security interest and/or "customer instructions prevail unless Bank elects otherwise," and omits absolute compliance covenant
Risk rating:        CRITICAL
Exposure analysis:  Without the statutory control agreement language, perfection by control may fail. Filing a UCC-1 against deposit accounts is generally ineffective as a perfection method (UCC § 9-312(b)(1)). Failure of control = unperfected security interest in Accounts, loss of priority to subsequent control parties and to the Bank, and potential adverse treatment in bankruptcy (strong-arm, adequate protection, cash collateral fights). Opinion counsel will not give a clean control opinion.
Recommended position: Require playbook control covenant verbatim (see aca-redline.docx § 2.2). No fallback that conditions compliance on Bank verification of default or joint instruction. Acceptable non-substantive tweak: Bank-standard authentication procedures for the identity of the Secured Party signer, without investigation of underlying default.
Fallback (client sign-off only): None on the core compliance covenant. At most, conform sentence structure to Bank standard form while preserving operative statutory elements.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 2 — Litigation-Conditioned or Judgment-Conditioned Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Provisions stating Pledgor retains dominion until Bank receives final non-appealable judgment / court order, or similar
Playbook requirement: Control and NOEC are contractual; no judicial precondition
Deviation:          Introduces litigation condition foreign to UCC control and to Credit Agreement remedies
Risk rating:        CRITICAL
Exposure analysis:  Renders exclusive control commercially useless during the period when Lenders most need it (default, restructuring, bankruptcy eve). Conflicts with self-help remedy structure of Article 9 and Credit Agreement acceleration/enforcement. Likely unacceptable to agent and required lenders; funding condition failure.
Recommended position: Delete in full. NOEC effective on Bank receipt per agreed notice mechanics.
Fallback:           None.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 3 — Joint Instruction / Dual-Signature Mechanics After NOEC
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Exclusive control article; payment order provisions
Playbook requirement: Post-NOEC, Bank complies solely with Secured Party instructions; Pledgor instructions cease
Deviation:          Requires joint Pledgor–Secured Party instruction after NOEC, or permits Pledgor counter-notice to stay exclusive control
Risk rating:        CRITICAL
Exposure analysis:  A hostile or unresponsive Pledgor can freeze collateral movement indefinitely. Defeats cash dominion and enforcement. Creates operational deadlock risk and leverage inversion in restructuring negotiations.
Recommended position: Delete dual-control and counter-notice stay. Only Secured Party may rescind NOEC (aca-redline.docx §§ 3.2, 3.4).
Fallback:           None on dual signature. Informational copy of NOEC to Pledgor is acceptable if failure to copy does not impair effectiveness (see Issue 7).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 4 — Unfettered Bank Setoff / Failure to Subordinate Bank Claims
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Banker's lien / setoff article; priority language
Playbook requirement: Bank subordinates all liens, setoff, and recoupment to Secured Party, except narrowly defined Banker's Liens limited to (i) customary account fees/charges, (ii) returned items/chargebacks, and (iii) ordinary-course overdrafts on the Accounts themselves — not other credit exposure
Deviation:          Preserves Bank setoff for "any obligations owing to Bank from time to time, whether or not related to the Accounts," and/or omits express subordination
Risk rating:        CRITICAL
Exposure analysis:  Under UCC § 9-327, a bank typically has priority as to deposit accounts at that bank unless it subordinates. Unsubordinated setoff can strip the account of value for other loans, derivatives, cards, or multi-product exposure, defeating the bargained-for collateral package. In a credit stress scenario at a relationship bank, this is a direct dollars-out-the-door risk equal to the full account balance plus ongoing deposits.
Recommended position: Full subordination with limited Banker's Liens only (aca-redline.docx §§ 2.5, 5.1). Cap fee-related liens to a short lookback (30–90 days) and require notice to Secured Party before post-NOEC setoff exercise.
Fallback (HIGH residual risk — client/agent approval): Permit Banker's Liens to also cover reasonable chargebacks for a short period; do not expand to unrelated credit products. If Bank is also a Lender, coordinate with Credit Agreement pro rata / setoff provisions but do not allow ACA to expand Bank priority beyond Loan Document bargains.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 5 — NOEC Only Upon Event of Default; Bank as Default Gatekeeper
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     NOEC delivery conditions
Playbook requirement: Secured Party may deliver NOEC at any time (or at any time permitted by the Credit Agreement, including springing dominion triggers that may precede a full Event of Default). Bank has no duty or right to verify EOD.
Deviation:          NOEC permitted "only following an Event of Default that is continuing," sometimes with Bank entitlement to demand evidence of EOD
Risk rating:        CRITICAL (if Credit Agreement has springing dominion) / HIGH (even in pure EOD-trigger structures, Bank verification is unacceptable)
Exposure analysis:  Misaligns ACA with Credit Agreement cash management architecture. Bank disputes over "whether a default exists" create fatal delay. Agent cannot operationalize dominion on Excess Availability / Dominion Event triggers.
Recommended position: NOEC at Secured Party's election; Bank relies on face of NOEC without investigating underlying circumstances (aca-redline.docx §§ 2.3, 3.1, 3.3). Whether Secured Party is contractually permitted vis-à-vis Pledgor to issue NOEC is a Loan Document matter, not a Bank condition.
Fallback:           Recital that Secured Party intends to issue NOEC in accordance with Loan Documents — expressly non-condition to Bank honor.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 6 — Pledgor Advance Notice / Cure Period Before NOEC Effective
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     NOEC effectiveness; cure rights baked into ACA
Playbook requirement: No ACA-level cure period that delays Bank exclusive compliance; Pledgor notice/cure lives in Credit Agreement if at all
Deviation:          X Business Days' prior notice to Pledgor before NOEC may be delivered or before Bank must honor
Risk rating:        HIGH
Exposure analysis:  Creates a race-to-empty-the-account window after default is known. Directly undermines cash collateral preservation. Inconsistent with typical Credit Agreement remedy immediacy post-EOD (subject to any negotiated CA cure periods, which should not be duplicated or extended in the ACA).
Recommended position: Delete ACA cure/advance-notice condition to Bank honor. Optional concurrent informational copy to Pledgor (Issue 7).
Fallback:           Same-day informational email to Pledgor; effectiveness vs. Bank remains on receipt.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 7 — NOEC Form, Delivery Method, and Effectiveness Timing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Notices article; NOEC form requirements
Playbook requirement: Email/PDF NOEC to dedicated Bank ops contact effective on a defined short timeline (same Business Day / next Business Day outside); commercially reasonable authentication OK; wet-ink certified-mail-only is unacceptable
Deviation:          Original wet-ink only; certified mail exclusive; multi-day deemed receipt; or undefined "when Bank has processed internally"
Risk rating:        HIGH
Exposure analysis:  Multi-day lag is a cash leakage window. Undefined "processing" time is a priority/operations dispute generator. Opinion and agency desks expect clear receipt rules.
Recommended position: Adopt aca-redline.docx §§ 3.1, 8.1 and Exhibit A. Permit email to Schedule II ops contacts; outside effectiveness not more than one Business Day after actual receipt if Bank form requires implementation lag; require written receipt confirmation within one Business Day.
Fallback:           Accept Bank standard callback/authentication for subsequent wires, separated from NOEC recognition timing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 8 — Incomplete Account Schedule; "Accounts as Customer May Designate"
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Schedule I; definition of Accounts
Playbook requirement: Specific account numbers, titles, types, currencies, branch/ABA, jurisdiction; amendments to Schedule I require Secured Party consent and Bank acknowledgment; no open-ended "designate from time to time" without control attach steps
Deviation:          Blank/incomplete Schedule I; floating account definitions; Pledgor may add/remove accounts unilaterally
Risk rating:        CRITICAL (if Schedule I blank at signing) / HIGH (if floating without consent)
Exposure analysis:  Control attaches to identified accounts. Blank schedules create identity failure for perfection and for opinions. Floating accounts without a signed amendment pathway leave new accounts unperfected by control.
Recommended position: Complete Schedule I from account-details checklist before signing; require Secured Party consent + updated Schedule I for changes (aca-redline.docx § 2.1 and Schedule I). Attach bank screen-print annex.
Fallback:           Post-closing tight deadline (e.g., 5 Business Days) only if pre-funding condition otherwise satisfied by escrowed signature pages and confirmed account list in funds-flow — not preferred.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 9 — Account Titling; UCC Jurisdiction; Account Characterization Reps
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Account setup; Bank reps
Playbook requirement: Title evidences security interest where Bank conventions allow (e.g., "Pledgor — Agent, as Secured Party"); Bank reps that Accounts are deposit/securities accounts, Bank is bank/securities intermediary, and Bank's jurisdiction for UCC §§ 9-304 / 8-110 / 9-305 matches opinion jurisdictions (typically NY); no consumer accounts
Deviation:          Untitled or Pledgor-only title; silence on jurisdiction and characterization; no consumer-account negative
Risk rating:        HIGH
Exposure analysis:  Jurisdiction mismatches break perfection analysis and opinions. Mischaracterization (e.g., unsecuritized "other" product) can take the arrangement outside §§ 9-104/8-106. Consumer accounts raise regulatory and UCC scope issues.
Recommended position: Insert § 2.1(c)–(d), § 2.4(d), § 6.2 playbook reps; confirm NY (or agreed) jurisdiction in writing with Bank.
Fallback:           If Bank refuses special titling, ensure control agreement language and customer-status analysis still support control under § 9-104(a)(2); document Bank convention in memo to file; do not concede jurisdiction rep.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 10 — Termination and Resignation; Account Closure
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Termination article
Playbook requirement: Termination primarily by Secured Party release on Payoff / commitment termination, or tri-party agreement; Bank resignation only on adequate prior notice (e.g., ≥30 days) with continued compliance during notice period and transfer per Secured Party Entitlement Orders; no unilateral Pledgor termination or closure without Secured Party consent
Deviation:          Pledgor may terminate or close accounts freely; Bank may terminate on short notice "for any reason" without transfer-of-control protections; automatic termination on account closure
Risk rating:        HIGH
Exposure analysis:  Loss of control mid-facility without replacement ACA = sudden unperfection. Short Bank exit without directed transfer enables cash migration outside the collateral package.
Recommended position: Adopt aca-redline.docx Article VII. Require replacement control mechanics before effective Bank resignation.
Fallback:           Bank resignation notice floor of 30 days; mandatory cooperation covenant; Secured Party direction of transfer. Reject Pledgor unilateral termination while Obligations outstanding.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 11 — Secured Party Indemnity of Bank (Joint/Several with Pledgor)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Indemnity / limitation of liability
Playbook requirement: Pledgor primary indemnitor; Secured Party indemnity, if any, limited to Secured Party's own gross negligence/willful misconduct, actual direct damages only, consistent with agent exculpation in Credit Agreement; no Secured Party liability for ordinary Bank fees/chargebacks
Deviation:          Secured Party indemnifies Bank on same terms as Pledgor; joint and several fee responsibility; consequential damages exposure
Risk rating:        HIGH
Exposure analysis:  Administrative Agent faces uncapped contingent liability misaligned with agency economics and Credit Agreement indemnity structure. Potential non-pro-rata exposure vs. Lenders; agency acceptance risk.
Recommended position: aca-redline.docx § 5.3. Push all ordinary indemnity to Pledgor. Cap any residual Secured Party exposure tightly.
Fallback:           Mutual limited indemnity for a party's own gross negligence/willful misconduct only; exclude consequential/punitive; no fee liability for Secured Party.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 12 — Expansive Secured Party Representations
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Representations article
Playbook requirement: Secured Party reps limited to due authorization of signatory (and possibly binding obligation of Agent in its capacity). No reps on Credit Agreement enforceability, borrower solvency, non-contravention of Lender agreements, or similar
Deviation:          Full corporate/enforceability/non-contravention package imposed on Secured Party
Risk rating:        MEDIUM–HIGH
Exposure analysis:  Inappropriate for administrative agent; creates footprint liability and potential bring-down issues at amendment/NOEC time.
Recommended position: Strip to authorization rep (aca-redline.docx § 6.3).
Fallback:           Add "to the knowledge of the executing officer" qualifier only if Bank insists on one additional baseline rep — still avoid CA enforceability.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 13 — Governing Law and Forum Mismatch
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Miscellaneous
Playbook requirement: NY law aligned with Credit Agreement and UCC opinion jurisdictions; Manhattan forum; jury waiver consistent with CA
Deviation:          Bank home-office law and exclusive local venue; or silence creating conflicts
Risk rating:        HIGH (if conflicts with opinion jurisdictions) / MEDIUM (venue only)
Exposure analysis:  Perfection choice-of-law errors; split litigation; opinion qualifications.
Recommended position: NY governing law with UCC perfection carve as in § 1.1 definition; NY forum and jury waiver (aca-redline.docx §§ 9.1–9.2).
Fallback:           NY law mandatory; limited Bank local-venue carve solely for collection of its fees — document in deviation matrix if granted.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 14 — Amendments Without Secured Party Consent
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Amendments; account terms incorporation
Playbook requirement: Amendments to ACA require written agreement of Bank, Pledgor, and Secured Party; Bank–customer account agreements cannot override control, priority, setoff subordination, or exclusive-control mechanics
Deviation:          Bank and Customer may amend account agreements freely; ACA incorporates Bank deposit agreement "as amended from time to time" without priority savings clause
Risk rating:        HIGH
Exposure analysis:  Side amendments can silently gut control (e.g., new setoff terms, revised instruction hierarchy).
Recommended position: Tri-party written amendments only (§ 9.3). Savings clause: deposit agreement governs ordinary operations only to the extent not inconsistent with the ACA; ACA controls in conflict on control/priority/NOEC/setoff.
Fallback:           Bank may update purely operational fee schedules with notice, subject to § 5.2 caps post-NOEC.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 15 — Successor Administrative Agent
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Assignment
Playbook requirement: Automatic recognition of successor Administrative Agent under Credit Agreement upon notice and customary evidence; no Bank consent right that can block agency succession
Deviation:          Assignment requires Bank consent or full re-papering as condition to recognition
Risk rating:        HIGH
Exposure analysis:  Blocks CA-mandated agent replacement; holdover agent problems; enforcement friction.
Recommended position: aca-redline.docx § 9.4(b).
Fallback:           Bank right to require specimen signature list update within a short period post-succession, without suspending NOEC honor to the successor once notice is given.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 16 — Information Rights / Account Statements
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Bank duties
Playbook requirement: Secured Party receives statements and, on request, balance/transaction detail, concurrently with Pledgor or promptly on request; Pledgor authorizes disclosure
Deviation:          Silence, or Secured Party access only post-NOEC / only with Pledgor consent each time
Risk rating:        MEDIUM
Exposure analysis:  Blinds agent to cash position pre-default; impairs borrowing-base / liquidity monitoring if Accounts are reporting accounts.
Recommended position: aca-redline.docx § 4.4.
Fallback:           Monthly statements automatically; ad hoc detail within 2 Business Days of request; electronic portal access if available.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 17 — Fees and Post-NOEC Debits
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Fees
Playbook requirement: Disclosed fee schedule; post-NOEC, no unrestricted debit for fees without Secured Party consent (ordinary maintenance fees may be capped exception)
Deviation:          Open debit authority at all times; undisclosed fees; ACA "setup fees" payable by Secured Party
Risk rating:        MEDIUM
Exposure analysis:  Balance erosion post-default; surprise costs to agent.
Recommended position: Schedule III disclosure; § 5.2 debit rules.
Fallback:           Fixed monthly maintenance debit cap post-NOEC; other fees invoiced to Pledgor.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 18 — Standard of Care vs. Liability Standard
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Bank duties / liability
Playbook requirement: Performance standard of commercially reasonable care (or care used for similar commercial accounts); monetary liability may be limited to gross negligence/willful misconduct if consistent with Bank form, without eroding Articles II–III duties
Deviation:          Gross negligence standard used to excuse ordinary non-compliance with NOEC/entitlement orders
Risk rating:        MEDIUM–HIGH (if it dilutes control duties) / LOW–MEDIUM (if limited to damages measure)
Exposure analysis:  Ambiguity invites Bank argument that ordinary failures to implement NOEC are uncompensated and perhaps unenforceable in practice.
Recommended position: Separate performance duty from damages standard (aca-redline.docx §§ 4.2, 5.3(d)).
Fallback:           Accept GN/WM damages limitation if absolute compliance duty for NOEC remains express and specific performance/injunctive concepts are not waived.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 19 — Force Majeure
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Bank protective provisions
Playbook requirement: Operational force majeure acceptable with commercially reasonable resumption efforts and prompt notice to Secured Party
Deviation:          Open-ended excuse without notice/resumption covenant, potentially including staffing or internal system choices
Risk rating:        MEDIUM
Exposure analysis:  Extended unexplained non-performance during stress periods.
Recommended position: aca-redline.docx § 4.6.
Fallback:           Bank standard FM list plus prompt notice and efforts covenant.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 20 — Securities Account / Article 8 Add-On
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Missing or incomplete if any Account is a securities account
Playbook requirement: If securities accounts are included: securities intermediary status, financial assets treatment, entitlement order compliance, jurisdiction under § 8-110
Deviation:          Deposit-account-only form used for brokerage/securities accounts, or silence
Risk rating:        CRITICAL (if securities accounts are in scope without Article 8 mechanics) / N/A (if purely deposit)
Exposure analysis:  Wrong statute = control failure for security entitlements.
Recommended position: Confirm account type on Schedule I; if securities, insert § 9.12 and related definitions.
Fallback:           Separate securities account control agreement on Bank/broker standard form modified to playbook, rather than forcing a deposit-only form.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 21 — Loan Document Status; Conflict Rule; Irrevocability
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Draft location:     Miscellaneous / missing
Playbook requirement: ACA is a Loan Document as between Pledgor and Secured Party; CA/SA control conflicts as between them; Pledgor agreements irrevocable while Obligations outstanding; Bank not charged with full Loan Document knowledge except as noticed
Deviation:          Silence, or "entire agreement" that could be read to supersede Security Agreement grant mechanics; revocable instruction powers
Risk rating:        MEDIUM
Exposure analysis:  Interpretive disputes; Pledgor revocation arguments; expense/indemnity path gaps.
Recommended position: aca-redline.docx §§ 9.6, 9.10, 9.13.
Fallback:           Conflict rule + irrevocability even if "Loan Document" label is negotiated into CA definitional amendment later.
